item.title: Covington City Council approves amendments for vendor permits
item.description: The Covington City Council voted unanimously to approve amendments for temporary commercial use permits at their Feb. 16 meeting.

item.title: CARROLL: A little dab'll do ya
item.description: A few months ago, we reminisced about cough drops, baby aspirin and various medications from days gone by. That opened the floodgates. Many readers shared memories of products we rarely see today. Let's take a trip down the aisles of the supermarkets of our childhood.

item.title: HARRIS: Financial Focus: Tax-saving moves you can still make for 2025
item.description: Tax season is upon us, and while April 15 may seem like it's right around the corner, you still have time to make some strategic moves that could lower your 2025 tax bill. Whether you're looking to reduce your taxable income or set yourself up for a more secure financial future, these options are worth considering.

item.title: NCS students Selected for GMEA District Honor Band
item.description: Newton County Schools has announced the students from across the district who have been selected to participate in the Georgia Music Educators Association (GMEA) District Honor Band — a distinguished ensemble representing some of the most accomplished young musicians in the region.

item.title: City of Porterdale approves 2026-31 Comprehensive Plan
item.description: In a unanimous decision, the City of Porterdale approved its 2026-31 Comprehensive Plan during a special-called meeting on Feb. 19. The city has been working on its latest Comprehensive Plan – which is a tool often used by local government officials to make future decisions – since April 2025.

item.title: Newton Lady Rams go to Buford and eliminate the Lady Wolves once again
item.description: For the second consecutive year, the Newton Lady Rams took the trip north to slay the Lady Wolves in Buford Arena. Despite big games from Buford’s best scorers, the Lady Rams were too much to handle in a 64-59 win in the Sweet 16. When it was all said and done, Zoey Jackson’s 18 points served as the catalyst for Newton to put an end to Buford’s 26-game win streak and its season.

item.title: Eastside comes up short in overtime thriller against Pace Academy
item.description: For the second year in a row, the Eastside Eagles boys basketball season has ended in heartbreaking fashion. The Eagles faced the No. 1 seeded Pace Academy Knights in what could be considered as one of the premier games of the entire season for Newton County basketball. A 21-point performance from MVP candidate Christian Gatewood led the Eagles to an impressive underdog performance against the Knights, who had not lost a game this entire calendar year.

item.title: Bryant and Whitmer excel as Alcovy routs Berkmar 15-3
item.description: The Berkmar Patriots proved to be no match for Trey Bryant and Alcovy as the Tigers earned a commanding 15-3 win on Wednesday. The game only went five innings, but the Tigers did damage in every single one.

item.title: Newton Rams begin region play with series sweep over Heritage Patriots
item.description: A three-game sweep was in order for the Newton Rams this past week as they started Region 4-AAAAAA with three straight wins over the Heritage Patriots. Despite three games in four days, the Rams showed no signs of slowing down as the team accumulated 26 runs in the series.

item.title: Sen. Raphael Warnock visits Social Circle to voice opposition to ICE facility
item.description: In anticipation of the implementation of a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility in Social Circle, the city received a visit from U.S. Sen. Raphael Warnock. Warnock, a Democrat who has represented Georgia in the U.S. Senate since 2021, met with Social Circle Mayor David Keener and Social Circle City Manager Eric Taylor to take a guided tour through the city’s drinking water and wastewater treatment sites.
